issues.t: Rear brakes grinding from stuck outer pads
issues.sym: Squeaking or grinding from the rear, with the outer rear pads worn down while the inner pads look nearly new.
issues.why: Road salt rusts the outer rear pads so they bind and keep the brakes lightly applied. Mazda released modified pads and clips through a service bulletin.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes inspected and ask a Mazda dealer about the bulletin repair. Do not ignore grinding, which can damage the rotors.

issues.t: Driver mirror glass shakes at highway speed
issues.sym: The driver-side mirror glass vibrates at higher speeds, blurring the view behind.
issues.why: The power mirror glass mount allows vibration. Mazda issued several service bulletins with a repair.
issues.next: Ask a Mazda dealer about the mirror vibration bulletin.

issues.t: Windshield cracking without impact
issues.sym: A crack appears in the windshield with no clear rock strike.
issues.why: Early CX-5 windshields were the subject of a lawsuit, and Mazda set up a customer service program for certain vehicles built in early 2013.
issues.next: Replace the glass if the crack is in your view or spreading, and ask a Mazda dealer whether your VIN was in the program.

issues.t: Rust and paint blisters on the liftgate
issues.sym: Bubbling paint or rust spots on the lower liftgate panel or around the liftgate stopper.
issues.why: Paint was applied too thin in these areas. Mazda issued service bulletins for the repair.
issues.next: Have a Mazda dealer inspect it and ask about the bulletin before the rust spreads.

issues.t: Liftgate may fall closed (recall)
issues.sym: The liftgate won't stay up or drifts down on its own.
issues.why: The liftgate support struts can corrode internally and lose their strength.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have both struts replaced. Don't stand under a liftgate that won't stay open.

issues.t: Overheating or no heat with code P011A
issues.sym: Check engine light, the engine running hot, or the heater blowing cold air.
issues.why: Mazda issued a service alert for a temperature-reading fault on these years that can show up as overheating or poor heat.
issues.next: Have the code read and the cooling system checked. Stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs high.

issues.t: Front strut bolts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front suspension over bumps or a change in handling.
issues.why: The bolts holding the front struts to the steering knuckles may not have been tightened properly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the inspection done soon. Have any new clunk from the front checked before driving further.

issues.t: Fuel filler pipe can rupture in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs in normal driving.
issues.why: In a rear collision the fuel filler pipe could be damaged and leak fuel, raising the risk of fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done.

issues.t: LED daytime running lights failing (recall)
issues.sym: One or both LED running lights go out or flicker.
issues.why: Moisture can get into the headlight assembly and damage the LED running light circuit.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; Mazda will inspect and replace the gasket or headlight as needed.

issues.t: Mazda Connect screen ghost touches, freezing and reboots
issues.sym: The infotainment screen registers touches by itself, freezes, keeps rebooting, drops Bluetooth calls, or the backup camera image fails to appear.
issues.why: Hardware and software faults in the Mazda Connect system led to a class action settlement that added extended coverage.
issues.next: Ask a Mazda dealer for the latest software and whether your screen qualifies for repair under the settlement coverage.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may not deploy properly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs.
issues.why: The side curtain airbags may not unfold correctly in a crash, reducing protection.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the airbags replaced promptly.

issues.t: Misfire or stalling from cylinder deactivation fault (recall)
issues.sym: Check engine light, misfire, loss of power, or the engine stalling and not restarting.
issues.why: Engine computer software could mishandle the valve adjusters when switching back from cylinder deactivation, letting an intake rocker arm move out of place and hit other engine parts.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the engine computer updated. If the engine misfires or loses power, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Fuel pump may fail (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, hesitation, the engine stalling while driving, or not starting.
issues.why: The impeller inside the low-pressure fuel pump can crack and stop the pump.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the fuel pump replaced. A stall at speed is a crash risk.

issues.t: Cylinder head can crack and leak coolant on the turbo engine
issues.sym: Coolant level drops, you smell something sweet after a drive, there may be crusty residue near the exhaust side of the engine and the low coolant warning may come on.
issues.why: The cylinder head can crack around the exhaust manifold area, usually at a stud hole, and coolant seeps out there.
issues.next: Stop driving it if the coolant keeps dropping or the temperature climbs, and have the head inspected; Mazda's fix is a new cylinder head.

issues.t: Cylinder head can crack on the 2.5L engine
issues.sym: Oil or coolant seeping down the side of the engine, a low level between services, and sometimes a burning smell after driving.
issues.why: Cracks can form in the cylinder head casting, so oil or coolant escapes past it; Mazda released an updated head assembly.
issues.next: Have the leak traced before the level gets low, because running the engine short of oil or coolant will damage it.

issues.t: Check engine light with the thermostat stuck open
issues.sym: Check engine light, heat that takes a long time to come up in cold weather, and a temperature gauge that sits low.
issues.why: The thermostat can stick open so the engine never reaches its normal running temperature, and the computer stores a code for it.
issues.next: Have the thermostat replaced; a cold-running engine uses more fuel and wears faster, but it is not an emergency.

issues.t: Creak or clunk from the steering column
issues.sym: A creak, click or clunk from behind the steering wheel when you turn it, worst at low speed or when parking.
issues.why: A nut inside the steering column can loosen, so parts rub and knock as the column takes load.
issues.next: Have the column checked; it is usually a tightening or replacement job and should not be left to get worse.

issues.t: Click from the front brakes at low speed
issues.sym: A single click or light clunk from a front wheel as you pull away or stop, often only on the first stops of the day.
issues.why: The front pads can move slightly in their brackets, which makes a click when the brakes first take hold.
issues.next: Mention it at the next service; Mazda has a fix for the noise and it does not affect braking.

issues.t: Power liftgate can open on its own
issues.sym: The tailgate opens when nobody pressed anything, sometimes while the car is parked.
issues.why: A fault in the power liftgate control can trigger the open cycle without a command.
issues.next: Have it looked at and switch the power liftgate off in the menu until then, so your luggage is not left exposed.

issues.t: Chirp from the transmission on the third to fourth shift
issues.sym: A short chirp or squeak as the transmission shifts from third to fourth under light throttle.
issues.why: The way one clutch pack engages on that shift can make the noise; it does not mean the transmission is slipping.
issues.next: Have it confirmed at a service visit and keep an eye on the fluid; no repair is needed if it only chirps.

issues.t: Tapping or rattle from the valve train
issues.sym: A light tapping or rattle from the top of the engine, often loudest on a cold start and on newer cars.
issues.why: Clearances in the valve train can make the noise before parts fully bed in.
issues.next: Have it recorded at a service visit so it can be compared later; a tap that grows or comes with a warning light needs a closer look.

issues.t: Damp seepage at the water pump bleed hole
issues.sym: A small coolant stain or crust under the front of the engine, with the level staying where it should be.
issues.why: The water pump has a bleed hole that weeps a little coolant by design, which looks like a leak.
issues.next: Have it checked once to confirm the level is steady; pumps often get replaced for this when they do not need to be.

issues.t: Oil seepage on the engine front cover
issues.sym: A film of oil on the front of the engine or a few drops on the driveway, with no big drop in oil level.
issues.why: Oil can seep from the joint at the engine front cover.
issues.next: Have the source confirmed and the level checked at each fill; a slow seep can be monitored.

issues.t: Rear differential case can crack on all-wheel drive cars
issues.sym: An oily patch under the back of the car, a whine or hum from the rear at speed, or a warning about the all-wheel drive system.
issues.why: The rear differential case can crack and let its oil out, which then starves the gears.
issues.next: Have it inspected soon; running a differential dry ruins it and can lock up the rear wheels.
issues.sevReason: Differential case crack leaks fluid; not a wheel or axle separation.

issues.t: Infotainment screen blank or slow to start up
issues.sym: The centre screen stays black or takes a long time to come up after you start the car, and the radio and camera may be missing.
issues.why: Software in the infotainment unit can hang on start-up.
issues.next: Ask for the latest software update at your next visit; nothing else on the car is affected.

issues.t: Mist inside the headlight lens
issues.sym: A haze or fog on the inside of a headlight, usually after rain or a car wash, that clears slowly.
issues.why: Moist air gets into the headlight housing and condenses on the cool lens.
issues.next: Have it compared with Mazda's guidance at a service visit; light haze that clears is normal, water pooling is not.

issues.t: Musty smell or water from the cabin air filter
issues.sym: A damp, musty smell from the vents, and sometimes water where the cabin filter sits.
issues.why: The cabin air filter can get wet, and a wet filter grows the mould that causes the smell.
issues.next: Have the filter and its housing checked and the drain cleared; a fresh filter usually fixes the smell.

issues.t: Trailer wiring can melt against the muffler (recall)
issues.sym: Trailer lights stop working, or you see melted wiring near the rear of the car.
issues.why: The trailer hitch wiring harness can rest against the muffler, and the heat damages the wiring.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have the harness rerouted under the campaign before you tow again, since damaged wiring near heat is a fire risk.
